newsitem.title: JAPAN: ATHLETICS-GERMANY'S DORRE CRUISES TO THIRD OSAKA MARATHON WIN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GERMANY'S DORRE CRUISES TO THIRD OSAKA MARATHON WIN.

text.p: Defending champion Katrin Dorre of Germany cruised to an easy win in the 16th Osaka International Women's Marathon on Sunday.
Dorre, fourth in the Atlanata Olympics, left Japan's second-placed Mariko Hara behind in the final five kms to break the tape in 2 hours 25 minutes 57 seconds, a winning margin of 57 seconds.
The win, on a chilly and windy day, was the 21st marathon victory for Dorre, who came within 42 seconds of her personal best time set in 1994, when she won the Berlin marathon.
"It was a difficult race because of the winds but I was able to post a good time," Dorre said.
Hara, who finished third in the Tokyo International Women's Marathon in 1995, cut her best time by nearly two minutes with a 2:26:54 finishing time.
The race doubled as one of Japan's qualifiers for the world athletics championships next August in Athens.
Romania's Lidia Simon, sixth in the Atlanta Olympics, came third in 2:27:04.
Barcelona Olympic champion Valentina Egorova, the silver medallist in Atlanta, retired from the race shortly before the 35-km point.
